content.why: The four balanced-scorecard perspectives are financial, customer, internal business processes, and learning and growth. [II.C.1]

content.stem: Typical metrics used in the internal business processes perspective of the balanced scorecard include:
content.why: Typical metrics for the internal business processes perspective of the balanced scorecard include throughput, cycle time, unit cost, defect rates, and quality level. [II.C.1]

content.stem: Key performance indicators (KPIs) are measured, from the lowest to highest level, as:

content.stem: Which perspective provides shareholders with a direct line of sight into the health and well-being of the organization?
content.why: The financial perspective provides shareholders with a direct line of sight into the health and well-being of the organization. [II.C.1]

content.why: Effective KPIs align with business goals; have clear ownership; are predictive, actionable, transparent, balanced, linked, standardized, timely, and limited in number. [II.C.1]

how inputs and the process affect outputs.
the connection between statistics and process improvement.
content.stem: In Six Sigma, the concept of Y = f(X) refers to:
content.why: In Six Sigma, the concept of Y = f(X) refers to a relationship in which the Y variable represents outputs and X represents the inputs. The function f represents the process that transforms the inputs into the outputs. By understanding this relationship, an organization can predict and control process outputs based on its inputs. [I.A.1]

informed of changes after the fact.
content.stem: A stakeholder whose daily work routine will likely be affected by a project should be:
content.why: A stakeholder whose daily work will be affected by a Six Sigma project should be included in relevant discussions and decisions. [II.A]

content.stem: A trucking company strives to improve its on-time delivery. In a staff meeting, it is reported that the on-time delivery rate has increased, and transportation costs have also increased due to trucks leaving the facility half-full. This is an example of:
content.why: Concentrating solely on the on-time delivery rate is an example of a suboptimized system. When improvements are proposed, it is important to think systemically, so that optimizing one metric will not result in the degradation of another. [II.C.1]

content.stem: One of the functions of key behavior indicators is to:
content.why: Key behavior indicators (KBIs) track behaviors that contribute to high-level performance, including cultural change in an organization. [II.C.1]

OKRs list objectives and the results required to achieve them.
OKRs cannot be used to track individual achievement.
content.stem: Which of the following statements is true about objectives and key results (OKRs)?
content.why: OKRs list objectives for either an organization, a department, or an individual, and then list the results that will be required to achieve the objective. [II.C.1]

content.stem: A customer satisfaction survey asks how likely respondents are to recommend the product on the standard 0–10 Net Promoter Score scale, where 0 is not at all likely and 10 is extremely likely. Based on the results shown below, what is the net promoter score?
content.why: Promoters (scores 9–10) = 23. Detractors (scores 0–6) = 5 + 4 + 1 = 10. Total respondents = 23 + 12 + 5 + 4 + 1 = 45. NPS = (promoters − detractors)/total = (23 − 10)/45 = 28.9%. [II.C.1]

content.stem: A company monitors the number of hits on its website sales page. This metric is likely a leading indicator of:
content.why: The number of hits on the company's sales page is likely a leading indicator of future sales. [II.C.1]

content.stem: Which balanced-scorecard perspective measures the efficiency, quality, and reliability of the internal processes through which the organization creates value?
content.why: The internal-business-process perspective measures the efficiency, quality, and reliability of the processes used to create and deliver value. The customer perspective addresses the customer value proposition. [II.C.1]

content.stem: Which perspective includes the capabilities and skills of an organization?
content.why: The learning-and-growth perspective includes the capabilities and skills of the organization and its people. [II.C.1]

content.stem: In five years, $5,000 will be available. Assuming annual compounding at 10% per year, to the nearest dollar, what is its present value today?
The net present value (NPV) of a project's cost is $100,000, and the NPV of its benefits is $750,000. What is the benefit-to-cost ratio?
content.why: Benefit-to-cost ratio = NPV of benefits/NPV of costs = $750,000/$100,000 = 7.5. [II.C.2]

content.stem: Costs associated with customer complaints are best characterized as:
content.why: Customer complaints occur after delivery and are external failure costs. The four cost-of-quality categories are prevention, appraisal, internal failure, and external failure. [II.C.2]

assign the stakeholder to another department.
cancel the project due to resistance.

content.stem: A current attitude assessment for a stakeholder shows that they are suspicious of the project. The project leader should:
content.why: When a stakeholder is suspicious of a project, the project leader should develop an action plan that reduces opposition and increases support rather than excluding or avoiding the stakeholder. [II.A]

content.stem: To the nearest dollar, what is the present value of a $15,000 cost incurred in three years at a continuously compounded annual rate of 4.0%?
content.why: With continuous compounding, PV = A exp(−rt) = $15,000 exp[−(0.04)(3)] = $13,303.81, which rounds to $13,304. [II.C.2]

content.stem: Using the cash flows shown, calculate the discounted return on investment (ROI) at an annual discount rate of 5%. Define discounted ROI as the present value of net benefits divided by the present value of costs.
To the nearest dollar, calculate the present value of a $300,000 payment that will occur at the end of Year 1, assuming an annual interest rate of 4%, compounded quarterly.
content.why: With quarterly compounding, the quarterly rate is 0.04/4 = 0.01 and there are four quarters. PV = $300,000/(1 + 0.01)⁴ = $288,294. [II.C.2]

content.stem: Product A sells for $55.50 and its total cost is $15.00. What is its gross margin percentage, defined as (selling price − total cost)/selling price × 100%?
content.why: Percentage margin = (revenue − cost)/revenue × 100% = ($55.50 − $15.00)/$55.50 × 100% = 72.97%, which rounds to 73%. [II.C.2]

content.stem: A two-month improvement produced $40,000 in gross benefits and required a $25,000 implementation cost. Using simple ROI = (benefit − cost)/cost × 100%, what is the project ROI?
content.why: For this short-term project, simple ROI = (benefit − cost)/cost = ($40,000 − $25,000)/$25,000 = 0.60, or 60%. [II.C.2]

content.stem: What is one of the most frequently cited causes for team failure?

content.why: Communication outside the team should occur regularly. It can take the form of a bulleted status report or presentation. Typical items include accomplishments, problems, issues or concerns, actions being taken, and 30-day plans. [III.B.3]

content.stem: Which leadership style provides clear instructions and combines high directive behavior with low supportive behavior?
content.why: The directing style combines high directive behavior with low supportive behavior and suits an enthusiastic beginner who has low competence but high commitment. [III.B.4]

content.stem: A leader who empowers process improvement team members to function independently is using which leadership style?
content.why: The delegating leadership style is characterized by low directive and low supportive behavior. It is suited for individuals who possess high competence and high commitment. Such individuals are often described as self-reliant achievers. They are proficient in their task and are highly motivated about it. [III.B.4]

content.stem: What type of leadership is best suited for team members with average competence and moderate commitment?
content.why: The supporting leadership style is characterized by low directive and high supportive behavior. It is suited for individuals who possess mid-competence and moderate commitment. Such individuals are often described as capable, but cautious, performers. They know their task but are not motivated about it. [III.B.4]

compare the current state to best-in-class processes or products.
improve processes using teams of five to seven employees.
restructure an entire organization and its processes.

content.stem: Which leadership characteristics are best used for team members with low competence but high commitment?
content.why: For team members who have low competence but high commitment, a directing leadership style is best. This style is characterized by low supportive but high directive leadership. [III.B.4]

content.why: Coaches work with individuals to develop skills and abilities. They also work with teams to help projects stay on track by providing resources for completion of team member assignments. content.stem: In a team meeting, one member continually has private conversations with the person next to them. This type of disruptive team member is known as the:
content.why: The whisperer has private conversations with the person next to them during meetings, distracting others and sometimes creating concern about side comments. [III.C.1]

content.stem: A team member who agrees with whomever they are currently speaking with and views decisions as a way to get ahead is known as the:

content.why: A team leader or facilitator can get the team back on track by using a redirect technique. [III.C.1]

content.stem: A team member is uncooperative and unassertive. They are exhibiting which type of conflict management behavior?
content.why: In the avoiding approach to conflict management, the participant hopes the problem will go away. It is used when team members are uncooperative and unassertive. [III.C.1]

content.stem: A team is having trouble generating ideas for improvement. The team facilitator can spark the team's creativity by using which technique?
content.why: A facilitator can use the idea-floating method to spark the team's creativity. [III.C.1]

content.stem: In which role in a RACI model must a decision be discussed with the individual before a final decision is made?
content.why: The RACI model is a matrix that lists stakeholders and tasks, and then indicates who is responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed for each task. A stakeholder in the "consulted" role must be asked about a decision before a final decision is made. [IV.C.4]

content.stem: A prioritization matrix was created by a team to choose which software product to purchase. Each criterion was ranked from 1 = best to 4 = worst. Based on the completed matrix, which product should the team consider first?
content.why: Compute each weighted rank using the stated weights: A = 4(0.50) + 3(0.25) + 1(0.25) = 3.00; B = 3(0.50) + 1(0.25) + 2(0.25) = 2.25; C = 1(0.50) + 2(0.25) + 4(0.25) = 2.00; D = 2(0.50) + 4(0.25) + 3(0.25) = 2.75. Because rank 1 is best, the lowest total is preferred, so Product C should be considered first. [IV.D.4]

content.stem: Using the precedence table below, identify the activities on the critical path.
content.why: There are three paths through the network: ACF = 5+8+6 = 19 days, BDF = 10+2+6 = 18 days, and EF = 15+6 = 21 days. EF is the path with the longest duration and is therefore the critical path. [IV.D.5]

content.stem: Using the precedence table below, what is the early start time for Activity C?
content.why: Activity C's only predecessor is Activity A, which runs from day 0 to day 5. The early start for Activity C is therefore equal to the early finish of Activity A, which is 5. [IV.D.5]

options: There is no effect on the finish date.

The project will finish at least five days late.
content.stem: Using the precedence table below, Activity E is delayed by five days. What effect will this have on the overall project timeline?
content.why: Activity E sits on the critical path (EF, at 21 days). Delaying any activity on the critical path delays the entire project by the same amount, so the project will finish at least five days late even if every other activity stays on schedule. [IV.D.5]

the latest that activity can finish without delaying the project.
the slack time for the activity.

content.stem: A Black Belt is preparing a simple random sample. List the steps, from first to last, that they must perform to take the sample. 1. Select the members of the population associated with the n random numbers. 2. Determine the sampling frame. 3. Generate a random sample of n different numbers between 1 and N. 4. [V.B.3]

content.stem: In measurement systems, the term accuracy encompasses which two components?
content.why: In measurement systems analysis, the term accuracy encompasses both bias and linearity. [V.C.1]

content.stem: The stability of a measurement system refers to its:
content.why: The stability of a measurement system refers to its accuracy and precision over time. The stability can be monitored using control charts. [V.C.1]

The scale cannot discriminate between conforming and nonconforming assemblies.

content.stem: A scale can weigh an assembly to the nearest pound. The weight specifications are 5 kg ± 0.6 kg. Use 1 lb = 0.454 kg and a 10:1 resolution-to-tolerance guideline. What can be said about the instrument?
content.why: The scale's 1 lb resolution is about 0.454 kg, while the 1.2 kg tolerance width calls for much finer discrimination (about 0.12 kg under a 10:1 guideline). Measurements near 4.4 kg or 5.6 kg can round across a specification boundary, so the scale cannot reliably distinguish conforming from nonconforming assemblies. [V.C.1]

options: Measurement-system variability is too large relative to the tolerance.
The measurement system is adequate for process control.
content.stem: A precision-to-tolerance ratio is calculated to be 0.50. Under standard measurement-system acceptance guidelines, what conclusion is justified?
content.why: A precision-to-tolerance ratio (PTR) is a measure of the capability of the measurement system. PTR values less than 0.10 are considered good, while values greater than 0.30 require improvement in the measurement system in terms of reducing its variability. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Which of the following individuals does not generally attend regular Six Sigma project team meetings?

content.why: Variance contribution is σ²(GRR)/σ²(total), the square of the fractional study-variation ratio σ(GRR)/σ(total). If gage R&R is expressed as a percentage, %Contribution = (%GRR)²/100. [V.C.1]

content.stem: If the bias of a measuring system increases across the measurement range, the measuring device is said to have poor:
content.why: If the bias of a measuring system increases across the measurement range, it is said to have poor linearity. A system with good linearity will have a constant bias across the range of measurement. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Which quadrant of the figure shows high precision but low accuracy?
content.why: The quadrant in the lower right (D) shows an example of high precision. It is consistent (tightly clustered) but not accurate since the points are not at the target. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Which quadrant in the figure shows high accuracy and low precision?
content.why: The quadrant in the upper left (A) shows a system with high accuracy, since the points average out near the target, but low precision because their locations are not consistent. [V.C.1]

content.stem: What is the measurement system concept depicted in the figure below?
content.why: The figure depicts the concept of linear bias: the average of measured values runs parallel to the true/reference value line but is consistently offset from it across the full range of measurement. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Using PTR = 6σ(total)/(USL − LSL), calculate the precision-to-tolerance ratio for specifications 10 ± 0.5 cm and σ(total) = 0.045 cm.
A measurement system has been evaluated with the following results: repeatability = 0.81 and reproducibility = 5.15. What is the gage R&R?
content.why: Gage R&R combines repeatability and reproducibility: GRR = √(EV² + AV²) = √(0.81² + 5.15²) = 5.21. [V.C.1]

content.stem: The gage R&R for a measurement system is equal to 3.45. The equipment variation is found to be equal to 1.22. What is the appraiser variation?
content.why: GRR² = EV² + AV², so AV = √(GRR² − EV²) = √(3.45² − 1.22²) = 3.23. [V.C.1]

content.stem: The standard deviation due to repeatability is also known as:
content.why: Repeatability is also known as equipment variation. It measures the precision under conditions where independent measurement results are obtained with the same method on identical items by the same appraiser using the same equipment within a short period of time. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Ignoring integer truncation, use NDC = √2[σ(parts)/GRR]. If NDC = 7.00 and gage R&R = 0.40, what is σ(parts)?
content.why: Using NDC = √2[σ(parts)/GRR], σ(parts) = NDC × GRR/√2 = 7.00(0.40)/√2 = 1.98. [V.C.1]

working with the team leader and facilitator to move the team toward the objective.
content.stem: The team coach for an improvement project is usually responsible for:
content.why: Coaches work with the team leader and facilitator to move the team toward the objective and help provide resources for completing team-member assignments. Additionally, they evaluate the team's progress. [III.A.2]

content.stem: A single operator measures 30 parts two times each. The average range of the readings is 2.45 mm. For two trials, use K₁ = 0.8862. What is the standard deviation due to repeatability?
content.why: Equipment variation (EV), the standard deviation due to repeatability, is EV = R̄ × K₁. Therefore, EV = 2.45 × 0.8862 = 2.171 mm, which rounds to 2.17 mm. [V.C.1]

content.stem: Two operators measure three parts two times each. Their average measurements are 45.67 cm and 47.54 cm, and equipment variation is 1.25 cm. For two operators, use K₂ = 0.7071. What is the appraiser variation?
content.why: Appraiser variation is the reproducibility component. Using AV = √[(Xdiff × K₂)² − EV²/(nr)], with Xdiff = 1.87, K₂ = 0.7071, EV = 1.25, n = 3 parts, and r = 2 trials, AV = √[(1.87 × 0.7071)² − 1.25²/(3 × 2)] = 1.22. [V.C.1]

content.stem: What components comprise total observed study variation?
content.why: Total observed study variation combines part-to-part variation with gage R&R. Gage R&R is the measurement-system component and combines repeatability and reproducibility. [V.C.1]

content.stem: ABC Manufacturing performed a gage R&R study on a pair of calipers used to measure the width of a part. The customer has since changed the specifications on the drawing for the width. What part of the gage R&R is likely affected when a new gage R&R study is performed?
content.why: The calipers used for measurement have not changed, so it is not expected that the components of gage R&R will be affected by the change in specifications. However, the percent tolerance ratio will be affected. [V.C.1]

content.stem: A random sample of n = 20 observations is taken from a population with μ = 34.5 and σ² = 4.5. What is the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean?
content.why: The population standard deviation is σ = √4.5. The standard error of the mean is σ/√n = √4.5/√20 = 0.474. [V.D.2]

content.stem: What theorem explains why the sample mean of independent observations is often approximately normally distributed and therefore supports use of an X̄ chart?
content.why: The central limit theorem states that, for independent observations from a population with finite mean and variance, the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches normality as the sample size increases. This supports plotting subgroup means on an X̄ chart even when the individual observations are not perfectly normal. [V.D.2]

content.stem: One hundred independent observations are taken from an exponential distribution with mean 2.0 and variance 4.0. The observations are summed. What is the approximate distribution of the sum?
content.why: By the central limit theorem, the sum is approximately normal with mean nμ = 200 and variance nσ² = 400. [V.D.2]

content.stem: A random sample of n = 40 independent observations is taken from an exponential distribution with scale parameter β = 2. Which distribution approximates the sampling distribution of x̄?
content.why: For an exponential distribution with scale β = 2, the population mean is 2 and variance is 4. With n = 40, the central limit theorem makes the sampling distribution of x̄ approximately normal, with mean 2 and variance 4/40 = 0.10. [V.D.2]

content.stem: The measure of the heaviness of a distribution's tails is known as:
content.why: The measure of the heaviness of a distribution's tails is its kurtosis. This measure is often mistakenly thought to represent the peakedness of a distribution. [V.D.3]

content.stem: The skewness of a distribution is equal to −2.3. What is the shape of the distribution?
content.why: A negative value of skew implies that the distribution is skewed to the left. [V.D.3]

content.stem: Given the sample data {94, 91, 76, 43, 66, 77, 55, 27, 50, 60}, what is the value of the sample mean?
content.why: The sample mean is the sum of the values divided by n: 639 / 10 = 63.9. [V.D.3]

content.stem: An effective Six Sigma project team member:
content.why: Effective team members actively participate in meetings, communicate ideas and expertise, listen openly, and complete action assignments as scheduled. [III.A.3]

content.stem: For the sample data {94, 91, 76, 43, 66, 77, 55, 27, 50, 60}, the sample mean is 63.9. What is the sample variance?
content.why: Sample variance is the sum of squared deviations from the mean divided by n − 1: Σ(xᵢ − 63.9)²/9 = 4048.9/9 = 449.9. [V.D.3]

content.stem: When a quick measure of dispersion is desired, which statistic can be used?
content.why: The range is a measure of dispersion that can be obtained with minimal calculation. [V.D.3]

content.stem: Given the following sample data {155, 161, 152, 161, 153}, calculate the sample median.
content.why: To find the median, we sort the data from low to high and choose the middle value: {152, 153, 155, 161, 161}. [V.D.3]

content.stem: Given the sample set of data {13.3, 14.5, −4.0, 23.9, 24.2}, calculate the standard deviation.
Given the sample data {17.0, 14.5, 2.5, 4.5, 12.3}, calculate the standard error of the mean.
content.why: The sample standard deviation is s = 6.34. The standard error of the mean is SE = s/√n = 6.34/√5 = 2.84. [V.D.3]

content.stem: Calculate the mean using the frequency table shown below.
content.why: Use each class midpoint to compute the grouped-data mean. The weighted sum is 19.5(14) + 39.5(10) + 59.5(5) + 79.5(4) = 1,283.5, and the total frequency is 33. Therefore, x̄ = 1,283.5/33 = 38.89. [V.D.3]

content.stem: Calculate the interquartile range using the box plot shown below.
content.why: The interquartile range is the difference between the third and first quartiles. The middle 50% of the data is contained between these two quartiles. The upper boundary of the box denotes Q3 and the lower boundary denotes Q1. (25 − 15) = 10. [V.D.4]

content.why: The box plot shows that the data are right-skewed and that the mean is greater than the median. The data value 170 is an outlier. [V.D.4]

content.stem: Which of the following graphs can be used as a quick check for normality?
content.why: A histogram shows the center, spread, and shape of a distribution and can be used as a quick check for normality. [V.D.4]

content.why: A scatter plot shows the relationship between two quantitative variables. Based on the scatter plot, the analyst can assess the nature and direction of the relationship and the correlation between the variables. [V.D.4]

make decisions using an authoritative approach.
content.stem: When choosing team members, it is important to select those who:
content.why: Effective team members should be open to change. Other important selection factors include the ability to influence others, subject-matter expertise, availability, and a team-oriented attitude. [III.A.3]

content.stem: Given the frequency table below, what is the cumulative frequency associated with X = 6?
content.why: Cumulative frequency at X = 6 is the running total through that row: 10 + 12 + 14 = 36. [V.D.4]

content.why: The ordered observations track the fitted straight line and remain within the 95% pointwise envelope, so a normal model is reasonable for these data. [V.D.4]

content.stem: Interpret the normal probability plot shown below (Plot 2).
content.why: The ordered observations curve away from the fitted normal line, with many values near zero and a long upper tail. This is the characteristic pattern of a right-skewed distribution, so a normal model is not appropriate. [V.D.4]

content.stem: Metal plates are inspected for two types of defects: burrs and scratches. A Black Belt calculates the probability of finding a burr or a scratch on a metal panel. Which probability rule would they use?
content.why: Let Event A = a burr and Event B = a scratch. The probability of A or B is found with the addition rule. [V.E.1]

content.stem: A project team consists of twelve members. How many ways can members be chosen for a three-member subcommittee?
content.why: Because order does not matter, use combinations: C(12,3) = 12!/[3!(12 − 3)!] = 220. [V.E.1]

content.stem: A sample of three numbers is selected from the numbers 1 to 45, inclusive. How many different combinations are possible?
content.why: Because order does not matter, use combinations: C(45,3) = 45!/[3!(45 − 3)!] = 14,190. [V.E.1]

content.stem: When the occurrence of one event negates the possibility of another event, the events are referred to as:
content.why: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur at the same time. A light switch is either on or off; it can't be both. [V.E.1]

content.stem: If events A and B are independent, which statement is true about the conditional probability P(A | B)?
content.why: For independent events, knowing that B occurred provides no information about A, so P(A | B) = P(A). [V.E.1]

options: For a given n and r, the number of combinations is generally larger than the number of permutations.
Order is important for combinations but not for permutations.
Order is important for permutations but not for combinations.
For a given n and r, the number of permutations is always greater than the number of combinations.
content.stem: What is the main difference between a permutation and a combination?
content.why: For permutations, order matters; for combinations, it does not. For a given n and r, the number of permutations exceeds the number of combinations when r exceeds 1, while the counts are equal when r = 1. [V.E.1]

content.stem: An event affects the probability of another event occurring. The events are referred to as:
content.why: If Events A and B are dependent, the occurrence of Event A affects the probability of occurrence of Event B, and vice versa. [V.E.1]

content.stem: Which training topic most directly helps process-improvement team members understand group behavior and avoid personality conflicts and turf wars?
content.why: Team-building training helps members understand how teams work and which individual behaviors advance progress, reducing personality conflicts and turf wars. [III.A.4]

content.stem: An inspector sampled four circuit boards from a steady stream of production that is known to be 12% nonconforming. What distribution would they use to find the probability of selecting two nonconforming units in the sample?
content.why: Use a binomial model because each sampled board is classified as conforming or nonconforming, the nonconforming probability remains 0.12, and sampling from a steady production stream makes the trials reasonably independent. [V.E.2]

content.stem: Assume calls arrive independently according to a Poisson process at a constant mean rate of 2.5 calls per minute. What is the probability of fewer than 2 calls in the next minute?
content.why: The count is Poisson with mean λ = 2.5. “Fewer than 2” means X ≤ 1, so P(X ≤ 1) = exp(−2.5)(1 + 2.5) = 0.2873. [V.E.2]

content.stem: Which of the following distributions is continuous?
content.why: The normal distribution is continuous. The other distributions listed are discrete probability distributions. [V.E.2]

content.stem: An emergency department handles an average of 7.7 patients each hour on a Wednesday evening. Using the cumulative Poisson probabilities below, how many arrivals should the check-in desk plan for if it wants capacity to meet or exceed the 95th percentile?
content.why: For X ~ Poisson(7.7), choose the smallest capacity x for which P(X ≤ x) is at least 0.9500. P(X ≤ 12) = 0.9496 is still below 0.9500, while P(X ≤ 13) = 0.9739 exceeds it. Therefore, the desk should plan for 13 arrivals per hour. [V.E.2]

content.stem: A normally distributed process metric has mean 32.79 and standard deviation 4.12. Four percent of production is above the upper specification limit. Use P(Z ≤ 1.75) = 0.9599 ≈ 0.96. What is the upper specification limit?
content.why: The 96th percentile of the standard normal distribution is z ≈ 1.75. Converting to the process scale gives x = μ + zσ = 32.79 + 1.75(4.12) = 40.0. [V.E.2]

content.stem: Ten square yards of carpet are inspected for cosmetic defects. The probability of finding two or fewer defects can be expressed using which probability statement?
content.why: For a discrete probability distribution, "two or fewer" includes 0, 1, and 2. Therefore, the probability statement is Pr(X ≤ 2). [V.E.2]

content.stem: A process output is normally distributed with μ = 53.7 inches and σ = 7.59 inches. Use the standard normal value Φ(0.83) = 0.7967. What percentage of product will be larger than 60 inches?
For a normal distribution, a little more than two-thirds of the values lie between:
content.why: For a normal distribution, approximately 68.3% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, or μ ± 1σ. [V.E.2]

content.stem: Assume 10 independently sampled parts, each with constant defective probability p = 0.05. What is the probability of fewer than 3 defectives?
content.why: This is a binomial problem because each part is classified as defective or nondefective, the defective probability is constant, and there is a fixed number of independent trials. Fewer than three defectives means Pr(X ≤ 2). With n = 10 and p = 0.05, sum Pr(X = 0) + Pr(X = 1) + Pr(X = 2) to obtain 0.9885. [V.E.2]

content.stem: Two manufacturing lines produce a bioplastic sheet with a tensile strength requirement of at least 9 MPa. Using the convention N(μ, σ²), Line A tensile strength follows N(12.5, 2.56) and Line B follows N(11.5, 6.25). Which line has a lower yield?
content.why: Yield is the percentage of product that meets specifications. For Line A, P(X ≥ 9) = P[Z ≥ (9 − 12.5)/√2.56] = P(Z ≥ −2.19). For Line B, P(X ≥ 9) = P[Z ≥ (9 − 11.5)/√6.25] = P(Z ≥ −1.00). Since P(Z ≥ −2.19) is greater than P(Z ≥ −1.00), Line A has the higher yield and Line B has the lower yield. [V.E.2]

options: A sponsor with a vested interest in the project
A Yellow Belt in attendance at all meetings
Advanced statistical training for all team members
content.stem: Which of the following items can best contribute to team success?
content.why: A sponsor with a vested interest in the project can help remove barriers and roadblocks, thereby setting the team up for success. [III.A.4]

content.stem: Which distribution is used to test goodness of fit, association, and the standard deviation of the normal distribution?
content.why: The chi-square distribution is used to test goodness of fit, association, and the standard deviation of the normal distribution. [V.E.2]

content.stem: A sample is drawn without replacement from a finite population whose units are classified as conforming or nonconforming. Which distribution models the number of nonconforming units selected?
content.why: The hypergeometric distribution models the count of successes when sampling without replacement from a finite population. [V.E.3]

content.stem: A bivariate normal distribution has how many parameters?
content.why: A bivariate normal distribution has five parameters: two means (μ₁ and μ₂), two standard deviations (σ₁ and σ₂), and one correlation coefficient (ρ). [V.E.3]

content.stem: Which distribution is useful when modeling multiplicative data?
content.why: The lognormal is used to model multiplicative data. [V.E.3]

content.stem: An inspection procedure calls for sampling 5 items from a lot of 25. If no defective items are found, then the lot is accepted and shipped. What distribution would best model the probability of acceptance for a lot?
content.why: The hypergeometric would be used to find Pr(X = 0) in this case because we are sampling from a finite population and classifying items as pass or fail. [V.E.3]

content.stem: The Weibull distribution is useful when modeling what type of data?
content.why: The Weibull distribution is useful when modeling reliability data. The bathtub curve can be modeled using three Weibull distributions with varying parameters. [V.E.3]

content.stem: As parts are made, they are placed in trays that hold 30 parts. If a tray contains 6 defective parts and 2 parts are sampled from the tray, what distribution would be used to calculate the probability that both will be defective parts?
content.why: The hypergeometric distribution is used when sampling from a finite population in which sample units are characterized as pass or fail. In this case, the hypergeometric parameters are N = 30, D = 6, and n = 2. [V.E.3]

options: The probability that X is less than s is the same as the probability that X is greater than s.
The probability that a unit will function for at least 100 more hours is the same whether it has already run for 1,000 or 2,000 hours.
The probability that a unit will function for 1,000 hours is the same as the probability it will function for 2,000 hours.
The probability that a unit will fail at time t equals 0.632.
content.stem: Which statement is true concerning the memoryless property of the exponential distribution?
content.why: The exponential distribution is memoryless: the probability of surviving at least another s units does not depend on the elapsed lifetime t. Thus, P(X > t + s | X > t) = P(X > s). [V.E.3]

content.stem: What is the connection between the Weibull and exponential distributions?
content.why: The Weibull distribution reduces to the exponential distribution when its shape parameter equals 1. [V.E.3]

options: Decrease the variability of the process.
Move the process mean to the target.
Increase the width of the specification limits.
content.stem: A normally distributed, in-control process output has a Cp = 1.75 and a Cpk = 1.0. What action should the team perform first to improve the process?
content.why: The process potential, or Cp value, shows that the process is capable. The Cp value is comparable to a 5.25 process sigma. The Cpk value is not equal to the Cp value, indicating that the process is not centered at target. The first step the team should take is to move the mean to target, thus making Cpk = Cp = 1.75. After that, the team can work on reducing variation to further improve the process. [V.F.1]

content.stem: Which of the following factors is considered a demotivating factor for team members?
content.why: Changes in project scope can become a demotivating factor for a team. [III.B.1]

content.stem: Which of the following cases would be considered the most desirable in terms of the relationship of the specification to the process spread?
content.why: Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ) is a larger-is-better index. A process spread 6σ that is smaller than the specification width provides the most desirable listed relationship. [V.F.1]

content.stem: Of the following Cp values, which index is the most desirable?
content.why: The Cp value is a larger-the-better metric. The most desirable Cp index from those listed is 1.50, which is corresponding to a short-term process sigma level of 4.5. [V.F.1]

content.stem: Which of the following cases would result in a Cp index equal to 1?
content.why: Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ). Therefore, Cp = 1 when the process spread 6σ equals the specification width USL − LSL. [V.F.1]

content.stem: The numerator of the Cp formula is also referred to as:
content.why: The numerator of Cp, USL − LSL, is called the voice of the customer. The denominator, 6σ, is called the voice of the process. [V.F.1]

options: An error was made in the calculation.
The process mean is outside the specification limits.
The Cp value is less than 1.
The process variation is too large.
content.stem: What does a negative Cpk signify?
content.why: A negative Cpk means the process mean lies outside a specification limit. Cpk = min[(USL − μ)/(3σ), (μ − LSL)/(3σ)], so one branch is negative when μ is above USL or below LSL. [V.F.1]

content.stem: Using the process-data table and bias-correction factor shown below, what is the value of Cp?
Using the process-data table shown below, what is the estimated natural tolerance width?
content.why: Estimate σ as σ̂ = S̄/c₄ = 9.9/0.9869 = 10.03. The natural tolerance width is 6σ̂ = 6(10.03) = 60.19. [V.F.1]

The process is centered within the specification limits but is not capable.

content.stem: Using an organizational minimum capability criterion of Cp ≥ 1.33 and Cpk ≥ 1.33, which statement is true if Cpk = 0.85 and Cp = 1.10?
content.why: Both indices are below the stated 1.33 criterion, so the process is not capable. Because Cpk is less than Cp, the process is also off center. [V.F.1]

content.stem: Lencioni describes five dysfunctions of a team. Which dysfunction is considered the primary inhibitor of a successful team?
content.why: According to Lencioni, absence of trust is the primary dysfunction and a fundamental inhibitor of team success. Trust is the bedrock of a well-functioning team: members must feel comfortable sharing opinions and making mistakes. Without trust, the other dysfunctions cannot be overcome. [III.B.1]

content.stem: The Cp, Cpk, and Cpm indices are used to characterize:
content.why: Cp, Cpk, and Cpm characterize short-term capability. Pp and Ppk characterize long-term process performance. [V.F.1]

options: The location of the process mean relative to the specifications.
The distance between the process mean and the process target.
The distance between the process variability and the specifications.
content.stem: What information does the Cpm index incorporate that Cpk does not?
content.why: Cpm includes the distance between the process mean and the process target in its denominator. This distance is the process bias: Cpm = (USL − LSL)/[6√(σ² + (μ − T)²)]. [V.F.2]

content.stem: A process is analyzed over five months: the average is 45.67 and the standard deviation is 0.75. Specifications are 44.0 to 50.0. What is the value of Pp?
A process has an average of 45.67, a standard deviation of 0.75, and specifications from 44.0 to 50.0. What is the value of Ppk?
A process has Cp = 1.25. What is its corresponding short-term process sigma level?
content.why: The short-term process sigma level is 3Cp. Here, 3(1.25) = 3.75. [V.F.2]

check the normality of the data.
choose only the metrics that are performing best.

content.stem: One step in conducting a capability study is to:
content.why: When conducting a process capability study, make sure the process is stable, use 25–30 subgroups for your dataset, and then check the normality of the data. If the data is not normal, a transformation can be used before calculating capability. [V.F.3]

content.stem: Given the following information from an in-control p-chart, calculate the process capability: Σnp = 55 and Σn = 2,800.
content.why: The process capability from a p-chart is reported as its centerline: p̄ = Σnp/Σn = 55/2,800 = 0.0196, which rounds to 0.020. [V.F.4]

options: It is calculated using the same method as from a variables control chart.
It is equal to the width of specification limits divided by the width of the control limits.
It is equal to the control chart average.
content.stem: What statement is true about process capability calculated from an attributes control chart?
content.why: For attribute control charts, process capability is represented by the chart’s average or centerline—for example, p̄, np̄, ū, or c̄. [V.F.4]

options: Inattention to team results and lack of success
Fear of conflict and absence of trust
Avoidance of accountability and absence of trust
Lack of success and fear of conflict
content.stem: According to Lencioni, before lack of commitment can be addressed, which dysfunctions must be overcome?
content.why: According to Lencioni, fear of conflict and absence of trust must be addressed before lack of commitment can be overcome. [III.B.1]

content.stem: Given the following information from an in-control np chart, calculate the process capability. Σ(np) = 120, n = 200, and the number of subgroups is 20.
content.why: For an np chart, process capability is reported as the centerline: n̄p = Σ(np)/k = 120/20 = 6.0 defectives per subgroup. [V.F.4]

content.stem: Four stable processes are monitored using u-charts, with the capabilities shown below. Which process has the most desirable capability?
content.why: The process capability for a u-chart is expressed as the average number of defects per unit. Therefore, Process B has the most desirable capability. [V.F.4]

content.stem: A stable c-chart has 25 points plotted with the sum of defects equal to 38. What is the capability of the process?
content.why: For a c-chart, the process capability is the average number of defects per sample: c̄ = total defects/number of samples = 38/25 = 1.52. [V.F.4]

content.stem: What Box-Cox transformation is used to transform data from a Poisson to a normal distribution?
content.why: The square-root transformation is used to stabilize Poisson count data: Y = √X. [V.F.5]

content.stem: To calculate the process capability for nonnormal data, a Black Belt can first use which statistical tool to convert the data to the normal distribution?
content.why: The Johnson transformation is a technique to convert nonnormal data to a normal distribution. The process capability can then be calculated using the transformed data. [V.F.5]

options: the customers' willingness to accept defects.
the difference between the upper and lower specification limits.
six times the process standard deviation.
content.stem: Tolerance is defined as:
content.why: The tolerance is the difference between the upper and lower specification limits. [V.F.6]

content.stem: A total of 345 units were inspected and 15 were found to be defective. What is the percentage defective?
content.why: Percentage defective = (defective units/total units) × 100% = (15/345) × 100% = 4.35%. [V.F.6]

content.stem: A total of 54,012 units were produced, and 453 were found to be inoperable. What is the ppm defective?
content.why: PPM defective = (defective units/total units) × 1,000,000 = (453/54,012) × 1,000,000 = 8,387 ppm. [V.F.6]

content.stem: Units are each inspected for four types of defects. A total of 522 units were inspected with the results shown below. Calculate the defects per unit.
content.why: To calculate defects per unit, we sum the defects and divide by the total number of units inspected: dpu = total defects / total units = 55 / 522 = 0.105. [V.F.6]

content.stem: There are five different defect types that can be found on any one unit: weight, length, thickness, diameter, and tensile strength. Six hundred units were inspected, and 34 defects were found. What is the DPMO?
content.why: There are 600 units and 5 defect opportunities per unit, so DPMO = 34/(600 × 5) × 1,000,000 = 11,333. [V.F.6]

a method that uses new tools to solve process problems.
a project approach that uses six steps to reduce defects.
a quality method that emphasizes reducing waste.
content.stem: Six Sigma can be thought of as:
content.why: Six Sigma is a philosophy, an improvement methodology using DMAIC, and a statistical standard of quality. Under the conventional long-term model with a 1.5σ mean shift, Six Sigma corresponds to about 3.4 defects per million opportunities. Lean, by contrast, emphasizes reducing waste. [I.A.1]

content.stem: Team members working on a process improvement project struggle to understand the team's goal and its meaning for them individually. The team is likely in which stage of team development?
content.why: Forming is the stage in which members struggle to understand the team's goal and what it means for them individually. [III.B.2]

content.stem: Assume the number of defects on a unit follows a Poisson distribution with a mean of 0.04 defects per unit. What is the first-pass yield (FPY)?
content.why: Using a Poisson model with DPU = 0.04, first-pass yield is the probability of zero defects: FPY = P(X = 0) = exp(−DPU) = exp(−0.04) = 0.961. [V.F.6]

content.stem: Three thousand parts are produced. Thirty-five were sent out for rework and six were scrapped. What is the first-pass yield?
content.why: First-pass yield excludes units requiring rework or scrap: FPY = (3,000 − 35 − 6)/3,000 = 0.9863. [V.F.6]

content.stem: A process requires three steps operated in series. The first-pass yield (FPY) values for the steps are 0.99, 0.95, and 0.97. What is the rolled throughput yield (RTY)?
content.why: For steps in series, RTY is the product of the first-pass yields: RTY = 0.99 × 0.95 × 0.97 = 0.912. [V.F.6]

content.stem: A 3-sigma process output is normally distributed and centered at target. If the mean shifts upward by 1.5σ, what is the resulting yield? Use Φ(1.5) = 0.9332 and Φ(−4.5) ≈ 0.
content.why: After a +1.5σ shift, the specification limits are −4.5σ and +1.5σ relative to the shifted mean. Yield = Φ(1.5) − Φ(−4.5) ≈ 0.9332, or 93.32%. [V.F.7]

captures both within and between subgroup variation.

content.stem: Short-term capability:
content.why: Short-term capability is measured with Cp, Cpk, and Cpm. These indices provide a snapshot of process capability under short-term conditions. [V.F.7]

captures both within and between subgroup variation.
is often larger in magnitude than short-term measures.
content.stem: Long-term process performance:
content.why: Long-term performance indices such as Pp and Ppk use overall variation and therefore capture both within- and between-subgroup variation. Process stability is still important when interpreting any capability or performance index. [V.F.7]

content.stem: The four scatter plots below all show the relationship between the same two variables under different conditions. Which figure demonstrates negative correlation?
content.why: In Figure B, y decreases as x increases—the points trend downward from left to right, indicating a negative correlation. [VI.A.1]

content.stem: The four scatter plots below show different relationships between two variables. Which figure demonstrates a nonlinear relationship?
content.why: The points plotted in Figure D rise and then fall, suggesting a parabolic (nonlinear) relationship rather than a straight-line trend. [VI.A.1]

content.stem: Across 30 subgroups, an attributes chart's underlying data totals Σnp = 55 and Σn = 2,800. What is the centerline of the p-chart?
content.why: The p-chart centerline is total defectives divided by total inspected: p̄ = Σnp/Σn = 55/2,800 = 0.0196. [VIII.A.4]

content.stem: Across 30 subgroups, an attributes chart's underlying data totals Σnp = 55 and Σn = 2,800. Calculate the control limits of the p-chart using the average sample size.
content.why: The average sample size is n̄ = 2,800/30 = 93.3, and p̄ = 55/2,800 = 0.0196. The limits are p̄ ± 3√[p̄(1 − p̄)/n̄] = 0.0196 ± 3√[(0.0196)(0.9804)/93.3] = 0.0196 ± 0.0431. The negative lower limit is set to 0, giving [0, 0.0627]. [VIII.A.4]

content.stem: An np-chart is based on 78 nonconforming units across 25 subgroups, each containing 200 units. What are the lower and upper control limits of the np-chart?

content.stem: Which distribution is used to calculate the control limits of the np-chart?

content.stem: Each hour, 10 units are sampled and inspected for defects. After 25 time periods, the total number of defects equals 38. Using this information, calculate the control limits for a c-chart.
content.why: The average count is c̄ = 38/25 = 1.52. Therefore, LCL = c̄ − 3√c̄ = 1.52 − 3.70 = −2.18, which is set to 0, and UCL = c̄ + 3√c̄ = 1.52 + 3.70 = 5.22. The control limits are [0, 5.22]. [VIII.A.4]

content.stem: A u-chart has ū = 240/1,550 defects per unit. What are the lower and upper control limits for a subgroup of n = 20 units?

content.stem: A new electric vehicle is evaluated for its maximum range on a single charge. Five vehicles produced the mileage results {265, 252, 255, 260, 251}. Assuming mileage is normally distributed, test H₀: μ ≤ 250 versus H₁: μ is greater than 250 at α = 0.05. Use the one-tailed critical value t(0.05, 4) = 2.132.
content.why: Because the population standard deviation is unknown and n = 5, use a one-sample Student's t test. The sample mean is x̄ = 256.60 and the sample standard deviation is s = 5.86, so t₀ = (256.60 − 250)/(5.86/√5) = 2.52. Since 2.52 exceeds 2.132, reject H₀; the data provide evidence that the average range exceeds 250 miles. [VI.B.5]

content.stem: What might be the effect of using 2σ control limits on an X̄ chart?
content.why: Narrowing X̄-chart limits from 3σ to 2σ increases the false-alarm probability α from about 0.0027 to 0.0455. The in-control average run length is ARL₀ = 1/α, so it falls from about 1/0.0027 = 370 subgroups to 1/0.0455 = 22 subgroups. [VIII.A.4]

content.stem: A Black Belt conducts a hypothesis test using a Student’s t statistic and α = 0.05. The p-value is 0.325. Which statement is true?
content.why: Because p = 0.325 is greater than α = 0.05, there is insufficient evidence to reject H₀. A p-value does not give the probability that either hypothesis is true, and failing to reject H₀ is not the same as accepting or proving it. [VI.B.1]

content.stem: The time during which work is actively performed on a unit at a process step is defined as:
content.why: Touch time is the time during which work is actively performed on a unit. It should not be confused with the time required for a process cycle or with total end-to-end lead time. [V.A.1]

content.stem: After adjustments to a packaging line, a Six Sigma professional wants a 95% confidence interval for the mean fill weight with a margin of error of 1 g. The historical process standard deviation is σ = 3.5 g. Use z* = 1.96. What minimum sample size is required?
content.why: Use n = (z*σ/E)² = (1.96 × 3.5/1)² = 47.06. Round up to the next whole observation, giving n = 48. [VI.B.3]

A u-chart tracks:

content.stem: A process step in a PFMEA has an RPN of 96, a severity rating of 8, and an occurrence rating of 6. What is the detection rating?
content.why: RPN = Severity × Occurrence × Detection. Therefore, Detection = RPN ÷ (Severity × Occurrence) = 96 ÷ (8 × 6) = 2. [VI.C.2]

content.stem: Schedule boards, signage, and color-coded bins are examples of:
content.why: Schedule boards, signage, and color-coded bins are examples of visual management. [VIII.B.2]

content.stem: If a project stakeholder is deemed to have low influence and high importance, what behavior approach should the project leader adopt for this stakeholder?
content.why: If a project stakeholder is deemed to have low influence and high importance, the project leader should adopt the "protect, defend, and give voice" approach. [II.A]

content.stem: Which subgroup size would not be used for an X̄-R chart?
content.why: An X̄-R chart requires more than one observation per subgroup, commonly n = 2 to 10. For n = 1, use an I-MR chart or another appropriate individuals chart. [VIII.A.4]

content.why: Robust design aims to set control factors to minimize the effects of noise factors. [IX.C]

content.stem: A production supervisor runs a punch press line for a few extra hours to create backup stock "just in case." What types of waste have been created?
content.why: Running the line a few extra hours to build up inventory would create both overproduction and inventory waste. [VI.D.3]

content.stem: The amount of output that passes through a process in a specified period is defined as:
content.why: The amount of output that passes through a process in a specified period is throughput. [V.A.1]

content.stem: On an eight-hour shift, a process runs a total of 438 minutes due to a scheduled 30-minute shutdown for lunch and 12 minutes of downtime due to a broken clamp. What is the availability of the process?
content.why: Availability equals actual operating time divided by planned operating time. The 30-minute lunch shutdown is planned. Actual operating time = (8 × 60) − 30 − 12 = 438 minutes; planned operating time = (8 × 60) − 30 = 450 minutes. Availability = 438/450 = 0.9733. [VII.B.4]

content.stem: A quality engineer will test a simple random sample of lightbulbs from a population large enough to ignore the finite-population correction. What minimum sample size is required to estimate the defective percentage with a 3% margin of error at 95% confidence? No prior estimate is available; use p = 0.50 and z* = 1.96.
content.why: With no prior estimate, p = 0.50 gives the most conservative sample size. n = 1.96²(0.50)(0.50)/0.03² = 1,067.11, so the minimum whole-number sample that meets the margin of error is 1,068. [VI.B.3]

content.stem: An evaluation method that uses a three-dimensional miniature version of a solution is known as a:
content.why: The evaluation method that uses a three-dimensional miniature version of a solution is known as a physical model. [VII.C]

content.stem: In a two-level full-factorial design, the effect of Factor A is equal to 5.72. What is the corresponding coefficient for Factor A in the coded regression model?
content.why: The coefficient in the coded regression model for a full-factorial experiment will be one-half the factor effect. Here, 5.72 ÷ 2 = 2.86. [VII.A.6]

content.stem: In a balanced scorecard, which perspective includes the capabilities and skills of an organization?
content.why: In a balanced scorecard, the learning and growth perspective includes the capabilities and skills of an organization. [II.C.1]

content.stem: What experimental design technique would be used when an experiment will have to be conducted over the course of two days?
content.why: If an experiment must be conducted over two days, the analyst should use blocking to account for any additional variability introduced by different conditions day to day. [VII.A.2]

content.stem: A university institutes two-factor authentication for logging into its systems. This is an example of:
content.why: Two-factor authentication is an example of mistake-proofing. [VII.B.1]

move too slowly to implement changes.
content.stem: Which listed action is a common change-management error because it leaves the people responsible for implementation unable to execute?
content.why: A typical change-management error is assigning the change-management function to people who lack the resources to execute it. [I.B.2]

content.stem: What is the most common loss function used for a minimum tolerance?
content.why: For a minimum tolerance (for example, diameter greater than 2.1 cm), use the larger-the-better loss function. [IX.C]

Projects are open-ended, with no time constraint.
content.stem: A kaizen blitz is best used in which situation?
content.why: A kaizen blitz is best used when improvement opportunities are readily identifiable, when the risk of failure is small, and when projects are time-bound and clearly defined. [VII.B.3]

content.stem: A customer requires 320 units per day. The plant operates continuously for one eight-hour shift. What is the required takt time in minutes per unit?
content.why: Takt time = Time available / Units required = 480 min / 320 units = 1.5 min/unit. Takt time is the rate at which the process must produce units to meet customer demand. [V.A.1]

content.stem: Which design feature most directly improves fault diagnosis and serviceability?
content.why: Design for Maintainability includes features such as built-in self-diagnostics, which make faults easier to detect and service. [IX.B]

content.stem: Put the theory-of-constraints improvement steps in order: (1) Exploit; (2) Elevate; (3) Identify; (4) Repeat; (5) Subordinate.
content.why: The steps in the theory of constraints are, in order, identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, and repeat. [VII.B.4]

content.stem: The upper control limit on a p-chart varies over time. This is due to changes in the:
content.why: The upper limit of a p-chart changes based on the value of the sample size, n. Larger samples result in tighter limits. [VIII.A.4]

content.stem: Which of the following terms is considered the fourth stage in a Six Sigma maturity model?
content.why: The fourth stage in a Six Sigma maturity model is institutionalization. The five stages include (1) launch, (2) early success, (3) scale and replication, (4) institutionalization, and (5) culture transformation. [I.A.1]

content.stem: Which of the following terms is associated with the third stage in a Six Sigma maturity model?
content.why: Scale and replication. The five stages of Six Sigma maturity are (1) launch, (2) early success, (3) scale and replication, (4) institutionalization, and (5) culture transformation. [I.A.1]

content.stem: A process step changes the form, fit, or function of a product, is required by the customer, and is performed correctly the first time. This step is classified as:
content.why: A value-added activity changes the product or service in a way the customer requires, and it is performed correctly the first time. [V.A.1]

content.stem: The time from when a hospital patient is discharged until the room is ready for the next patient is known as:
content.why: The interval from patient discharge until the room is ready for the next patient is setup, or changeover, time. In manufacturing, it is the interval from the last unit of one job to the first good unit of the next job produced at full speed. [V.A.1]

content.stem: The unplanned rework, workarounds, inspections, and corrective activities that consume process capacity without adding customer value are collectively called the:
content.why: The hidden factory consists of unplanned work, such as rework, workarounds, inspection, and correction, that consumes resources without adding customer value. [V.A.1]

content.stem: A value stream map (VSM) is a detailed process map that shows what types of information?
content.why: A value stream map (VSM) shows process steps in sequence. It may include cycle and changeover times, staffing, WIP, inventory, packaging sizes, scrap rates, value-added and non-value-added activities, and changeovers. [V.A.2]

content.why: Work instructions should include labeled graphics; required parts, materials, tools, fixtures, and personnel; safety and defect risks; the exact sequence of steps; and a document and revision number. [V.A.2]

content.stem: A team would like to track the physical path that parts travel from arrival at the dock through the manufacturing process. Which graphical tool is the best choice?
content.why: A spaghetti diagram shows how parts or people physically move through a process. A gemba walk may be used to collect observations for the diagram, but it is not itself a graphical tool. [V.A.2]

content.stem: Which of the following measurements is considered discrete data?
content.why: The number of defects per unit is a count and therefore discrete data. Discrete data takes values from a finite or countably infinite set, such as the nonnegative integers. [V.B.1]

content.stem: Data collected on which measurement scale is classified into categories with no order implied?
content.why: Nominal data can be classified into categories, but there is no implied order. Numerical values used only as labels, such as identification numbers, are also nominal. Sums or averages of nominal labels are not meaningful. [V.B.2]

content.stem: On which measurement scale can data be ranked, even though precise differences between ranks are not defined?
content.why: Ordinal data has intrinsic order, but differences between ranks are not necessarily equal. For example, runners may finish first in 30 minutes, second in 31 minutes, and third in 45 minutes. [V.B.2]

content.stem: Which measurement scale has meaningful, equal differences and an absolute zero?
content.why: Ratio data has meaningful, equidistant differences and an absolute zero, so ratios are meaningful. For example, if Part A weighs 3 kg and Part B weighs 6 kg, Part B weighs twice as much as Part A. [V.B.2]

content.stem: What is an acceptable measure of dispersion to use for data that is on the ordinal measurement scale?
content.why: For ordinal data, acceptable measures of dispersion include the range and interquartile range. [V.B.2]

content.stem: A company creates a customer-satisfaction survey using a five-point Likert scale. Which measurement scale is associated with this type of data?
content.why: A Likert response scale is ordinal: responses are ordered, but the difference between adjacent categories is not guaranteed to be equal. [V.B.2]

content.stem: An injection-molding process has a four-cavity mold running in one press. What sampling method is most appropriate to monitor this process?
content.why: Sampling from every cavity ensures that each cavity is represented. Treating the cavities as strata is stratified sampling. [V.B.3]

content.stem: An internet poll reveals that respondents prefer Product A over Product B. This result is likely not representative of the population due to:
content.why: Self-selection bias occurs when individuals decide whether to participate. Those who choose to respond are often not representative of the population as a whole. [V.B.3]

content.stem: A quality inspector chooses every 10th assembly coming off the final production line for testing. What type of sampling scheme is being used?
content.why: Choosing every nth item in a sequence is systematic sampling. [V.B.3]

content.stem: A company sends a survey to its 2,400 customers. Using the finite-population planning formula n = N/(1 + NE²), what is the minimum number of responses required for E = 3.5%?
content.why: Using n = N/(1 + NE²), n = 2,400/[1 + 2,400(0.035)²] = 609.14. Round up to ensure the requirement, giving 610 responses. [V.B.4]

involve frontline workers affected by the project.
content.stem: Six Sigma projects should:
content.why: Six Sigma projects should involve the frontline workers of the process being improved. These workers are stakeholders in the project and have key insights into the process. Their support is needed for any improvements to stick. [I.A.2]

content.stem: What is the purpose of z-score standardization (called normalization in this guide)?
content.why: Z-score standardization places different data sets on a common unitless scale with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. It does not transform a nonnormal distribution into a normal distribution. [V.B.4]

content.stem: A useful tool for keeping a tally of events is known as a:
content.why: A check sheet is one of the seven basic quality tools. It is used to tally occurrences of defined events or categories, often over time. [V.B.4]

use as short a collection period as possible.
collect data during only one short, supposedly representative period.
content.stem: A data-collection plan for seasonal data should:
content.why: For seasonal data, the collection window should span several complete seasonal cycles. Regular sampling is useful, but a short window can miss the seasonal pattern. [V.B.4]

content.stem: What is the interpretation of the slope in a simple linear regression?
content.why: The slope is the expected change in the predicted response for a one-unit increase in x. The sign of the slope determines whether the predicted response rises or falls. [VI.A.2]

The regression model is overestimating the input variable.
content.stem: A simple linear regression model returns a negative residual for a particular value of X. What must be true about the model?
content.why: A residual is e = y − ŷ. If e is negative, then ŷ > y, so the model is overestimating the observed response. [VI.A.2]

options: Y is independent and normally distributed with a constant mean and standard deviation.
Errors are independent and normally distributed with mean 0 and constant variance σ².
X and Y are normally distributed and dependent.
Errors are dependent and normally distributed with mean 0 and variance σ²/n.
content.stem: What are the assumptions for simple linear regression?
content.why: Simple linear regression assumes independent errors with mean 0 and constant variance σ²; normal errors are required for exact small-sample inference. Residual plots are used to assess these assumptions. [VI.A.2]

content.stem: A 95% confidence interval on the response of a regression model will be at its narrowest point when which statement is true?
content.why: The confidence interval for the mean response is narrowest at X = x̄ because the leverage term (X − x̄)² is then zero. [VI.A.2]

options: At any given X, the confidence interval will be wider than the prediction interval.
The confidence and prediction intervals will be equal at X = x̄.
Both the confidence and prediction intervals will get wider as x deviates from its average value.
The width of the prediction interval is independent of the value of x.
content.stem: For a simple linear regression model, an analyst calculates 95% confidence and prediction intervals. What is true about these intervals?
content.why: Both intervals are narrowest at x̄ and widen as x moves away from the average observed x. A prediction interval is also wider than the corresponding confidence interval because it includes individual-response variation. [VI.A.2]

reduce the dimensionality of a data set when inputs are correlated.
categorize brainstormed ideas into natural groupings.
content.stem: The purpose of discriminant analysis is to:
content.why: Discriminant analysis develops one or more linear combinations of predictors that separate observations into two or more predefined classes. [VI.A.3]
